aliocha schneider.bio: Paris-born, Québec-raised singer-songwriter and actor Aliocha Schneider works in both French and English. His screen debut came in Bon Cop, Bad Cop (2006), followed by roles in Maman est chez le coiffeur (2008), Le Journal d'Aurélie Laflamme (2010) and Closet Monster (2015). Jean Leloup invited him to record with The Last Assassins before Schneider launched his solo music career with the Sorry Eyes EP in 2016, nominated for Best Folk EP at the 2017 GAMIQ Awards. His albums include Eleven Songs (2017), featuring the single "Flash in the Pan," Naked (2020), and the self-titled Aliocha Schneider (2023).

allan rayman.bio: Toronto-based singer-songwriter Allan Rayman pairs a gravelly voice with shadowy alternative R&B, folding in hip-hop, grunge and alternative rock. He broke through with Hotel Allan, self-released in 2015 and issued through Communion Music in 2016, the label co-founded by Mumford & Sons' Ben Lovett. Its follow-up, Roadhouse 01 (2017), built a narrative record around his "Mr. Roadhouse" alter ego. He earned a 2018 JUNO nomination for Breakthrough Artist of the Year. Further albums Harry Hard-on (2018), Christian (2020), Roadhouse 02 (2022) and The All Allan Hour (2024) followed, matched by a deliberately cryptic visual world.

andy shauf.bio: Andy Shauf is a Saskatchewan-born singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist known for detailed narrative songs. Born in Estevan and raised in Bienfait before settling in Regina, Shauf played drums in the Christian pop-punk band Captain before going solo, self-releasing early records and signing to Arts & Crafts in Canada and ANTI- internationally in 2015. His breakthrough came with the 2016 concept album The Party, a Polaris Music Prize shortlist finalist on which he played nearly every instrument himself. He followed it with The Neon Skyline (2020), earned multiple Juno nominations, and records with the band Foxwarren. He moved to Toronto in 2016.

boslen.bio: Vancouver rapper Boslen, born Corben Bowen, grew up in Chilliwack, British Columbia, and turned to music full-time after rugby injuries ended his University of Victoria scholarship, dropping out in 2018. That year he released the Motionless and Motionless II mixtapes, finding his sound on 2019's Black Lotus EP. He signed to Capitol Records and issued his debut album DUSK to DAWN in 2021, a cinematic alt-rap record mixing trap rhythms with rock, pop and punk energy and featuring Charmaine, Dro Kenji, Rascalz, Vory and Tyla Yaweh. He followed it with the GONZO EP on June 24, 2022.

connor price.bio: Connor Price is a Canadian rapper, actor, and internet personality from Markham, Ontario. He began performing at six and built a long acting career first, appearing as Jay Braddock in the film Cinderella Man (2005), as Kenny on Syfy's Being Human, and as Harry James on CBC's X Company. He turned to hip-hop in the late 2010s, releasing the debut project 4 of Clubs in 2018. In 2022 he released the singles "Spinnin," "Bankroll," and "Buddy," followed by the viral Spin the Globe series, in which he collaborates with an artist from whichever country his finger lands on, released as the Spin the Globe project (2023) and Spin the Globe 2 (2024). His debut studio album About Time arrived in 2025.

cri.bio: CRi is the stage name of Christophe Dubé, a Québec electronic musician and producer. He began as a beatboxer in the electro-hip-hop group Feuilles et Racines before launching his solo electronic project with a self-released EP in 2013. He signed to the UK label Anjunadeep in 2019. His 2020 debut album Juvenile, featuring the Daniel Bélanger collaboration "Signal," blended warm house grooves with French-language songwriting; it earned an Electronic Album of the Year nomination at the 2021 Juno Awards. In 2021 he was named Révélation de l'année (Breakthrough Artist) at ADISQ, and he followed up with the album Miracles (2023), featuring Half Moon Run and Klô Pelgag. His earlier EPs include Tell Her (2016) and Initial (2019); Someone Else (2017) earned a Juno nomination for Electronic Album of the Year in 2018.

dear rouge.bio: Dear Rouge are a Vancouver-based husband-and-wife alternative rock duo formed in 2012 by Danielle and Drew McTaggart. Both were touring musicians in other projects (Danielle in the duo Gaetz Ave, Drew in the band Maclean) when they met, married, and started the band, taking its name from Danielle's hometown of Red Deer, Alberta. After winning Vancouver's Peak Performance Project in 2012, their self-released single "I Heard I Had" became a Canadian radio hit and won the SOCAN Songwriting Prize. Following their major-label debut Black to Gold (2015), they won the Juno Award for Breakthrough Group of the Year in 2016. They followed it with PHASES (2018), Spirit (2022) and Lonesome High (2024).

dvsn.bio: dvsn (pronounced "division") are a Toronto R&B duo pairing vocalist Daniel Daley with producer Nineteen85 (Paul Jefferies). After releasing their first songs in 2015, they signed to Drake's OVO Sound label in 2016 and released the debut album Sept. 5th the same year, appearing on Drake's "Faithful" from Views. Their atmospheric slow jams continued on Morning After (2017) and A Muse in Her Feelings (2020), which featured collaborations with PARTYNEXTDOOR, Ty Dolla $ign, Summer Walker, and Jessie Reyez. They teamed with Ty Dolla $ign again for the joint album Cheers to the Best Memories (2021) and released Working on My Karma in 2022.

grandtheft.bio: Toronto producer and DJ Grandtheft is the recording alias of Aaron Waisglass, whose club-focused electronic music ranges from trap and moombahton to future house, informed by hip-hop, dancehall and bass music. By the early 2010s his career accelerated with releases on Mad Decent, Top Billin and Spinnin' Records, plus a Diplo collaboration remixing Calvin Harris's "Sweet Nothing." His Quit This City EP arrived in 2015 on Mad Decent. His 2014 Keys N Krates collaboration "Keep It 100" won a MuchMusic Video Award and appeared in the Minions movie trailer, and his 2016 single "Easy Go" with Delaney Jane followed.

justin nozuka.bio: American-born, Toronto-raised singer-songwriter Justin Nozuka built his name on intimate acoustic songwriting, releasing his debut Holly in 2007 after writing its songs as a teenager; Glassnote Records picked it up for its 2008 reissue, and Holly earned him a 2008 JUNO nomination for New Artist of the Year. Follow-up You I Wind Land and Sea (2010) topped Billboard's Heatseekers chart and earned a JUNO nomination for Adult Alternative Album of the Year, while Ulysses (2014) stretched his folk-soul palette further. Later releases, including 2023's Daydreams & Endless Nights, moved him toward lush alternative R&B, and he has performed on The Late Show with David Letterman.

kiwi jr..bio: Toronto band Kiwi Jr. plays jangly, literate guitar pop drawing on the slacker-pop lineage of the 1980s and 1990s. Formed in 2015, the band is built around Charlottetown, Prince Edward Island transplants Jeremy Gaudet (vocals, guitar), Brian Murphy (guitar), Mike Walker (bass) and Brohan Moore (drums), who moved to Toronto and began playing together. Their debut album Football Money (2019) on Mint Records introduced their wiry, hook-laden sound. They signed to Sub Pop for Cooler Returns (2021) and Chopper (2022), the latter produced by Dan Boeckner of Wolf Parade and Handsome Furs. They released their fourth album, Blowin' Up, in August 2026.

olivia lunny.bio: Winnipeg-born singer-songwriter Olivia Lunny picked up guitar at 12 and wrote her first song that year; at 14 she played the Winnipeg Folk Festival's Stingray Young Performers showcase. A 2018 Western Canadian Music Award nomination for Pop Artist of the Year recognized her early work. She was a winner on the second season of CTV's The Launch, and her 2019 single "I Got You" reached the Top 40. She signed with Universal Music Canada, launched her own Infinity & imprint, and received the SOCAN Foundation's Young Canadian Songwriter Award. Her catalogue runs from the EP To the Ones I Loved (2020) through her self-titled debut album (2021), the Heartbreak on Repeat EP (2023) and Velvet & Denim (2025), with alt-pop singles "Sad to See You Happy" and "Fix This."

aiza.bio: Aiza Ntibarikure, known as Aiza, is a Toronto-based singer-songwriter and actress born in Montreal to Burundian parents. Blending R&B and Afro-pop in both English and French, she released her debut album Sovereignty on September 29, 2023. Alongside music she has built an acting career: she plays superhero Sierra Ectoplex in Netflix's Jupiter's Legacy and Maya Bronté on CBC's Workin' Moms, voices Jazzy in the children's series Jeremy and Jazzy, and has had songs placed in series including Tuca & Bertie and Kim's Convenience.

alicia moffet.bio: Québec City-born pop singer-songwriter Alicia Moffet broke through by winning the 2013 season of YTV's The Next Star at 15, earning a chance to record a single licensed by Sony Music Canada. She released "Why Do Boys Lie" in 2014 and appeared on La Voix in 2015. After a string of independent singles in 2019, she released her debut album Billie Ave. in June 2020, named after her daughter, followed by Intertwine (2022) and No, I'm Not Crying (2025). Her bilingual catalogue moves between pop, R&B and folk-tinged ballads. In 2023 and 2024 she co-hosted the reality series Occupation Double.

anaïs cardot.bio: French-Gabonese singer and songwriter Anaïs Cardot was born in Libreville, Gabon and raised in the south of France, South Africa and Ottawa. Singing in English, French and Spanish, she blends soul, jazz, folk and bossa nova influences. Her 2020 single "Crazy for You" was followed by the Pink Magnolia EP in 2023 and the project Map of Her Shadow in 2026. Her collaborations include work with Nigerian stars Asake ("My Heart") and Wizkid ("Slow").

anna katarina.bio: Anna Katarina is a Vancouver-based Canadian-American singer-songwriter, multi-instrumentalist and producer. Trained in classical music from childhood, she studied at Selkirk College and Berklee College of Music, and performs on vocals, keys and guitar. Her solo work blends indie pop and rock with folk and soul; her debut solo album arrived in October 2022. She is also one half of the indie-folk duo Rumour Mill, whose work has received US college-radio play and screen placements in American film and TV.

anna sofia.bio: Toronto-area singer, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Anna Sofia emerged as a teenager writing candid songs about high-school life. She debuted with the single "Meaner Girl" in 2019 at 15, followed by "I Try" and "No Fun" and her debut EP Self Aware Bitch (2020) on Republic Records. Signed to Universal Music Canada, she released the Broken Perfection EP later that year, working with producers Jeff Hazin and Frank Dukes, and earning notice from Wonderland, Complex, American Songwriter and IDOLATOR. Drawing on '70s and '80s radio pop alongside electronica, hip-hop and lo-fi indie rock, she continued with the 2022 EP LET ME OUT I'M FREE! and later singles on Ultra Records.

anomalie.bio: Anomalie is the project of Montréal keyboardist, composer and producer Nicolas Dupuis, a classically trained pianist with a background in classical and jazz. His EPs Métropole (2017) and Métropole Part II (2018), inspired by his hometown, established his fusion of jazz-funk musicianship with groove-driven electronic production. He followed them with the Bend the Rules EP with Chromeo (2020), Galerie (2022) and Holidays (2023). Performing as Anomalie Live with a four-piece band, he has toured across North America, Europe and Asia and played Red Rocks, the Montreal Jazz Festival and Electric Forest. His early releases were self-released; he signed with Nettwerk in 2022.

aqyila.bio: Aqyila is a Toronto R&B singer-songwriter born Taahira Aquiyla Duff, an artist of Jamaican descent. Raised on gospel, reggae and R&B, she began uploading covers and originals online before "Vibe for Me (Bob for Me)" took off on TikTok in 2021. She signed with Sony Music Canada. Her debut EP For the Better (2023) featured "Hello," which won the 2024 JUNO Award for Traditional R&B/Soul Recording of the Year. The viral single "Bloom" followed in 2024, and her debut full-length Falling into Place arrived in March 2025.

ardn.bio: ARDN is a Burundian-Canadian rapper based in Edmonton, Alberta. He released his debut EP Goodwill in 2018 and followed it with ALIEN in 2020, building a name on introspective, melodic hip-hop. A snippet of "Til The Morning" went viral on TikTok in 2022. He signed to Capitol Records in 2023, releasing his major-label debut single "Plain Jane" that March. He toured across Canada and Europe opening for Isaiah Rashad. His 2025 album Keep Your Eye on the Sparrow earned a Juno Award nomination for Rap Album/EP of the Year at the Juno Awards of 2026.

arman ayva.bio: Arman Ayva is a Montreal-based composer and producer working in jazz-fusion, jazz-funk, ambient and electronic music. Of Armenian heritage, he has been experimenting with music since 2011, blending jazz-funk grooves with electronic textures and folk undertones. His influences include Marcus Miller and Dave Brubeck, and he releases independently through his own channels.

arpin lépine.bio: Québec singer-songwriter Arpin Lépine grew up in Saint-Félix-de-Valois, in the Lanaudière region. Blending country, rap and bluegrass with banjo, slide guitar and hip-hop-informed rhythms, he pairs rural storytelling with an unvarnished vocal style. He released the EPs DANS NOTRE COIN and Chance in 2025, followed by his debut solo album Lune Brune in January 2026.

asun eastwood.bio: Belize-born, Toronto-raised rapper Asun Eastwood is part of Canada's underground hip-hop scene and a member of the Brown Bag Money collective. Raised on Wu-Tang, he makes sample-driven boom-bap built on vivid storytelling and dense lyricism. His catalogue runs from the 2017 debut mixtape Hollywood Briggs through the Finn-produced With All Due Respect (2019) to collaborations with Futurewave and Daniel Son (Physics of Filth, Bite The Bullet), the Vago-produced Sewer Science (2020), and joint projects with Rochester's MAV and Toronto's Sibbs Roc.

charmaine.bio: Charmaine Willie, known as Charmaine, is a Zimbabwean-Canadian rapper based in Toronto. Her Warner Music Canada debut single, "Bold" (2020), won the Juno Award for Rap Single of the Year in 2022, the first year the category was presented as a standalone award. She followed it with her debut EP, Hood Avant Garde (2021), featuring "Bold" and "WOO!". Named a Spotify Canada RADAR artist and Amazon Music Canada's Breakthrough artist, Charmaine pairs assertive, high-energy flows with a strong R&B singing voice.

deadly alfano.bio: Deadly Alfano is the solo project of Toronto singer-songwriter Francesco Alfano, launched after years fronting the Toronto band Lucid Movement. His single "Shelter," released October 2, 2026, was produced by J.C. Sandoval of St. Doval, mixed by Andrew Lauzon at Hamilton's Grant Avenue Studio and mastered by Noah Mintz at Lacquer Channel. Alfano leads the live band on vocals and guitar, joined by Sandoval on bass, Trison Boyes on guitar and Adam Houle on drums.

desiire.bio: Desiire is a Toronto-based singer-songwriter born in Kinshasa, in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, who moved to Scarborough at 12. He began singing in his mid-teens, blending '90s R&B vocals with synth-pop and electronic production. His releases include the Starlight EP (2021). In 2020 he sang on ArtistsCAN's all-star rendition of "Lean on Me" for COVID-19 relief in Canada, alongside Justin Bieber, Bryan Adams, Avril Lavigne and others.

He began singing in his mid-teens, blending '90s R&B vocals with synth-pop and electronic production. His releases include the Starlight EP (2021). In 2020 he sang on ArtistsCAN's all-star rendition of "Lean on Me" for COVID-19 relief in Canada, alongside Justin Bieber, Bryan Adams, Avril Lavigne and others.

dirty radio.bio: DiRTY RADiO are a Vancouver dance-R&B band formed in 2010 by Farshad "Shadi" Edalat (lead vocals, percussion), Zachary "Waspy" Forbes (DJ, production) and Anthony "Tonez" Dolhai (mixing, production). Fusing progressive pop, R&B and electronic music, their albums include Debut, Cassette and Pleasures, alongside the Lick 1.0 EP and singles including "Numbers," "True Love" and "My Life." Their music has appeared on international labels including Spinnin' Records, Fool's Gold and Mad Decent, and they have shared stages with acts including Dragonette, Funk Hunters and Lights.

frvrfriday.bio: FRVRFRIDAY is the stage name of Tommy Ruhingubugi, a Rwandan-born Canadian singer, rapper and producer. Born in Rwanda and raised in Montreal from the age of two, he made his first beat on the family computer at 14 and released his debut single "Got It" in 2017, followed by the EPs More Than You Know and Offline and the six-track WHOISFRIDAY. His 2020 single "Window Shopping" featured Lil Baby, and his collaboration with fellow Canadian Anders, "What I Like," earned a nomination for Rap Single of the Year at the 2022 Juno Awards.

karim ouellet.bio: Karim Ouellet (1984–2021) was a Senegalese-born Canadian pop singer-songwriter based in Quebec City. Born in Dakar on December 8, 1984 and adopted by Canadian diplomats, he lived in France, Rwanda and Tunisia before his family settled in Quebec City when he was 15. He released his debut album Plume in 2011, then broke through with Fox (2012) and its hit "L'amour"; Fox won the Juno Award for Francophone Album of the Year in 2014. His third album, Trente, arrived in 2016, the same year as the Aïkido EP. His French-language pop blended folk, soul, reggae and electronic influences.

kellylee evans.bio: Scarborough-born singer-songwriter Kellylee Evans is a Juno Award-winning jazz and soul vocalist. Educated at Carleton University, where she earned degrees in law and English before turning to music full-time, she took second place at the 2004 Thelonious Monk International Jazz Vocals Competition. Her debut album Fight or Flight? (2006) earned a Juno nomination; her Nina Simone tribute Nina (2010) won the 2011 Juno for Vocal Jazz Album of the Year. Come On was released in France in 2015 and earned a 2018 JUNO nomination. After a lightning strike in 2013 and subsequent health setbacks sidelined her for several years, she returned to performing. She has opened for John Legend, Tony Bennett and Erykah Badu.

kimmortal.bio: Kimmortal is the professional name of Kim Villagante, a queer Filipino-Canadian musician, singer-songwriter and visual artist based in Vancouver. Raised in Surrey, British Columbia, Kim released a debut album Sincerity in 2014 and broke through with X Marks the Swirl (2019), which was longlisted for the Polaris Music Prize. Their music moves between rap, hip-hop, R&B, soul and experimental sounds, addressing race, gender, identity and community. Their original song "Made Up My Mind" for the series Sort Of won Best Original Song at the Canadian Screen Awards. They have opened for Thundercat, Saul Williams and Ruby Ibarra, and performed at SXSW and Junofest.

la sécurité.bio: La Sécurité are a Montreal dance-punk group bringing together musicians from the city's indie scene: vocalist Éliane Viens-Synnott, guitarists Melissa Di Menna and Laurence-Anne Charest-Gagné, bassist Félix Bélisle (Choses Sauvages) and drummer Kenny Smith. Their debut album Stay Safe! arrived in 2023 on Mothland and was longlisted for the 2024 Polaris Music Prize. They toured the United States in 2024 supporting The Go! Team, and released the remix EP Stay Safe! REMIXED the same year. Their second album, Bingo!, followed in June 2026 via Bella Union and Mothland.

magi merlin.bio: Montréal-based singer, songwriter and producer Magi Merlin calls her sound "Broken R&B," a self-built collision of indie pop, '90s house, R&B, hip-hop and jazz, co-produced with longtime collaborator Funkywhat. Raised in Saint-Lazare, she broke through with the 2022 EP Gone Girl, covered by Bandcamp Daily, The FADER, The Line of Best Fit and Nylon. She has toured with Noga Erez and Omar Apollo. A 2025 surprise EP, A Weird Little Dog, preceded a US run supporting Nubya Garcia. Festival appearances include Osheaga and FEQ, where she opened for Ty Dolla $ign. She made her acting debut in Chandler Levack's Mile End Kicks and released her debut album POWER HOUSE in July 2026.

plaza.bio: Toronto R&B singer and songwriter PLAZA, born Michael Kaminski, makes atmospheric alternative R&B built on hushed vocals and nocturnal, downtempo production. Before the alias, he fronted Toronto rock bands Lobby and Decades, re-emerging as PLAZA in 2016 with the independent EP One. Its late-night ballads caught the ear of Drake's OVO Sound, which signed him to a Warner-distributed deal; the five-track Shadow EP followed in 2017, highlighted by "Personal," alongside singles including "All Mine." After his OVO period he founded Shadow Records, returning in 2021 with "Still Alive" ahead of his debut album Nocturnes, released that October.

raahiim.bio: RAAHiiM is a Toronto R&B singer, songwriter and producer who records reflective ballads and slow jams with candid lyrics. Formerly performing as Raahiem, he released the EP Fear of the Unknown in 2017 before breaking through with the 2019 single "Peak (Fed Up)." His 2020 project ii KNEW BETTER was executive-produced by Nineteen85, and he has writing credits with dvsn. He followed it with BUT IF iiM HONEST (2023) and the twelve-track album PRAY FOR ME via MNRK Music Group. He has opened for Jessie Reyez on tour.

shay lia.bio: Shay Lia is a Montreal-based singer-songwriter and producer born Shanice Dileita Mohamed in France in 1993 and raised in Djibouti. She moved to Montreal for university, where posting singing videos online caught the attention of producer Kaytranada. She sang on his 2014 single "Leave Me Alone," later included on his Polaris and Juno-winning album 99.9%, and his 2018 single "Chances." Her solo work blends R&B, funk, house and electronic music: debut EP Dangerous (2019) was longlisted for the Polaris Music Prize, followed by the Afro-pop-leaning Solaris (2020).

shawnee kish.bio: Shawnee Kish is a Two-Spirit Mohawk singer-songwriter originally from Welland, Ontario. She broke through by winning CBC Music's Searchlight competition in 2020, followed by a place in the Allan Slaight Juno Master Class artist-development program in 2021. Her self-titled debut EP (2021) earned a Juno nomination for Contemporary Indigenous Artist of the Year; the follow-up, Revolution (2023), brought two more Juno nominations, including Adult Alternative Album of the Year. Her debut album, CHAPTER 1, arrived in 2025, marking a move toward country music and earning a 2026 Juno nomination for Contemporary Indigenous Artist or Group of the Year. Kish also created "Music Is My Medicine," a symphonic work performed by the National Arts Centre Orchestra.

sofia camara.bio: Sofia Camara is a Portuguese-Canadian singer-songwriter born on Terceira Island, Portugal in 2002 and raised in Toronto. She started writing songs at 13, busking in subway stations and posting covers of Taylor Swift and Justin Bieber online. Her first single with UMC/21 Entertainment, "Never Be Yours," arrived in 2022, before the 2024 viral single "Who Do I Call Now? (Hellbent)." Her debut EP, Was I(t) Worth It?, arrived in March 2025, followed by Hard to Love that October, featuring "Girls Like You," which reached the Top 10 of Billboard's Canada CHR/Top 40. She earned a 2026 Juno nomination for Breakthrough Artist or Group of the Year. Her EP Still Somewhere Here followed on October 9, 2026.

sophie powers.bio: Sophie Powers is the professional name of Sophie Anne Luborsky, a Toronto-born singer, songwriter and fashion designer now based in Los Angeles. She broke out with her debut EP Red In Revenge (2022), collaborating with Kellin Quinn and NOAHFINNCE, and followed it with Glitch: Lvl 1 (2024) featuring "Nosebleed." Her genre-blurring music combines hyperpop, pop-punk, electropop and hip-hop. In March 2025 she performed the joke song "STFU" on American Idol, and she also records under the side-project name Pixl Girl. She has performed at Slam Dunk Festival and Warped Tour.
